summary: Horst Lasic works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999, served as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995, and became a lecturer at Vienna in 1999.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served in epigraphy roles for the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and Government of India (~1920–1925), became Government Epigraphist for India in 1925, and lectured at the University of Calcutta.
Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim and earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo and served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.

Hoyo Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1958). He later served there as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1978–2004) and dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 1984–1985).
Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a linguist who studied at Getronagan Armenian High School, Faculty of Arts of Paris, University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann, and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University.

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University. Hu served as an associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Zhikai, Ruoshun, Shikai, and Yin Shun. He founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985), and held posts at Chinese Culture University and Tunghai University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Hsu Yun was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953 and served as its honorary president.
Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist and religious studies leader who studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, serving as its abbot (~1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held posts at Ohio University and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1974–2012).

Huai-Chin Nan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology who studied at the Republic of China Military Academy and University of Nanking under Huanxian Yuan. He held professorships at Chinese Culture University, National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. Chen completed a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong, studied under Stephen F. Teiser, and was an assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2007–2013).

Huanhuan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the University of Tokyo, and as a professor at Zhejiang University (attested 2015).
Huawen Bai was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1951–1955) and later served there as a professor (~1955–1999).

Hubert Decleer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Regent Hotel and Technical School, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte, later holding roles at the School for International Training from 1987.
